response.title: FY2027 Budget Request to Open a Sixth Harborlight Site
response.dek: Staff ask the board to approve a $1,610,000 budget for FY2027 to open a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and hire two site coordinators.

stat.label: Adults still on the waitlist when FY2026 ended

sections.heading: Five sites can't keep up
sections.body: Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in FY2026, up from 936 the year before. When the year ended, 287 adults were still waiting for a seat. Most were waiting at the Eastgate and Riverside sites, and the average wait was nine weeks.

sections.heading: What the money pays for
sections.body: The $1,610,000 FY2027 budget opens a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and adds two site coordinators. Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners each year. They also expect it to cut the waitlist in half.

sections.heading: Proof that the program works
sections.body: Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks rose one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential, the most in Harborlight's history. A team of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 hours.

sections.heading: Where FY2026 money came from
sections.body: Operating expenses came to $1,420,000, and 81 percent of spending went to programs. Foundation grants brought in $640,000, individual donors gave $388,000, and the city's adult education contract paid $295,000. Each learner cost $1,237 to serve.

points.text: The new site should serve 180 more learners each year
Learners wait nine weeks for a seat on average
Reserves are at 3.2 months, short of the 4-month goal

quote.text: I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring.
quote.who: A learner at the Riverside site

response.next: The board will vote on the FY2027 budget at its October 21 meeting.

chart.title: The FY2027 request is higher than FY2026 spending
